description: Refuse destroy, stop, and restart inside a sandbox (#1531), send the agro-release dispatch to agro-web after each release, and add execution location, directory, and fork CI rules to the delegate and git procedures.

userStories.title: Refuse `destroy`, `stop`, and `restart` inside a sandbox
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the guarded lifecycle verbs to refuse inside a sandbox so that an agent cannot wipe its own sandbox.
acceptanceCriteria: `runDestroy` in `.agro/cli/src/commands/lifecycle.ts` checks `runningInsideSandbox()` before `routeVerb`, the confirmation prompt, and any runner call.
`runComposeVerb` checks `runningInsideSandbox()` before `routeVerb` for the verbs `stop`, `restart`, and `destroy`.

Inside a sandbox, each of the three verbs writes `` `agro <verb>` manages the sandbox container from the host — you are already inside the sandbox. Run it on the host, at the project root. `` to stderr through `HostOnlyError`, returns 1, and makes 0 runner calls.
`agro ps` and `agro logs` keep their current behavior inside a sandbox.

Red tests in `.agro/cli/src/__tests__/lifecycle.test.ts` fail before the change and pass after the change. The destroy test reproduces #1531: `runDestroy({ bin: "agro", yes: true, name: "agro-sbx-1525-capture", ... })` inside a sandbox makes no runner call.
`pnpm run typecheck` exits 0. `pnpm test:scripts` exits 0.
userStories.notes: Integrated ff at 1a31b1cd. C1-C2 reasoned: diff shows runningInsideSandbox() as first statement in runDestroy and in runComposeVerb for HOST_ONLY_COMPOSE_VERBS stop/restart/destroy. C3 executed: lifecycle tests assert exact HostOnlyError message, return 1, 0 runner calls. C4 executed: ps and logs tests return 0 with one runner call. C5 executed: worker reported 4 red before, 8 green after; #1531 test uses agro-sbx-1525-capture. C6 executed: pnpm run typecheck exit 0; lifecycle.test.ts 122 passed on integrated branch.

userStories.title: Send the `agro-release` dispatch to agro-web after each release
userStories.description: As an operator, I want each AGRO release to trigger the agro-web docs sync so that the site shows the released docs.
acceptanceCriteria: The `finalize` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` ends with a step named `Notify agro-web of the release`.
The step sends `POST repos/mifunedev/agro-web/dispatches` with `event_type` `agro-release` and `client_payload.ref` equal to `v${{ needs.reserve.outputs.releaseVersion }}`.
The step reads the token from the secret `AGRO_WEB_DISPATCH_TOKEN`. The step prints a `::warning::` and exits 0 when the secret is empty.
A failed dispatch does not fail the release run: the step sets `continue-on-error: true` and prints a `::warning::` with the HTTP status.
A test in `.agro/scripts/__tests__/` asserts the step name, its position as the last step of `finalize`, the event type, the ref expression, and the secret name.
`CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` holds an entry for the dispatch and for the US-001 guard.
`pnpm test:scripts` exits 0.
userStories.notes: Integrated by cherry-pick as eb62afac (worker ef335820). Owned paths extended by the advisor to canonical-publish-contract.test.ts, whose whole-file regex blocked any later continue-on-error; the assertion now covers only the publish-cli job. C1-C5 executed: release-dispatch.test.ts asserts the last step name, POST dispatches, event_type agro-release, the v-prefixed release version ref, secret AGRO_WEB_DISPATCH_TOKEN, empty-token warning with exit 0, and continue-on-error true. C6 reasoned: Unreleased Changed and Fixed entries link #1536 and #1531. C7 executed: pnpm test:scripts exit 0 (112 files, 2808 passed) and build:harness exit 0 on the integrated branch.

userStories.title: Add execution location, directory, and fork CI rules to the procedures
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the procedures to state where each worker runs and who approves fork CI. Then no agent acts on infrastructure without consent.
acceptanceCriteria: The `## Dispatch record` table in `.agro/skills/delegate/SKILL.md` holds an `Execution location` row: `host` or `sandbox`. The advisor decides the value with `/etc/agro/sandbox`, or with `/.dockerenv` plus a non-empty `SANDBOX_NAME`.
The `## Worker brief` list holds a rule: in a sandbox, never run `agro sandbox`, `agro destroy`, `agro stop`, `agro restart`, or raw `docker compose` for the current project.
The `## Waves` section holds a rule: the advisor never sends parallel shell calls that change the working directory. Each parallel call uses absolute paths, for example `git -C <path>`.

`.agro/skills/git/SKILL.md` holds a rule for pull requests from a fork: an agent never approves an `action_required` workflow run, for example with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>/approve`. Only the operator approves a fork run. The agent verifies the fork change locally in the sandbox instead.
`bash .agro/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh .agro/skills/delegate/SKILL.md .agro/skills/git/SKILL.md` reports no finding on a changed line.
`bash .agro/scripts/link-providers.sh --check` exits 0.
userStories.notes: Integrated by cherry-pick as a42e3c95. C1-C3 reasoned: diff adds Execution location row (marker /etc/agro/sandbox, or /.dockerenv plus SANDBOX_NAME), worker-brief rule against host-only verbs in a sandbox, Waves rule against parallel calls that change directory. C4 reasoned: git SKILL.md PR Bodies rule reserves fork run approval for the operator. C5 executed: worker ran ste-check on both files, no findings before and after. C6 executed: link-providers.sh --check prints Providers OK on integrated branch.

userStories.title: Record the manual review evidence
userStories.description: As the advisor, I want test and workflow evidence for the three changes so that the PR `## Manual review` section shows the observed behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: `.agro/tasks/sandbox-guard-release-dispatch/evidence/manual-review.md` holds the command and output of the US-001 lifecycle tests and the US-002 workflow test.
The transcript holds the `git diff` of the US-003 skill change.
The advisor runs no `destroy`, `stop`, or `restart` command in the sandbox. A failed guard would stop the live sandbox, so the unit tests carry the proof.
